doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Evacuating to Baton Rouge; the flooded house
summary: Evacuating to Alvin Batiste's house and the state of his flooded home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Yeah I had to go to Baton Rouge with Alvin Batiste. He was living in New Orleans, he was working at a house in New Orleans and his home was in Baton Rouge. So we evacuated to his house. We had about twelve people in his house at the beginning. And eventually I got me an apartment I think the second week in Baton Rouge so half of the family moved out and my daughter, she was with me, and then she found an apartment in Baton Rouge. So I’m still in Baton Rouge and I got a trailer in New Orleans.

My house is completely messed up. Well we were in the process the week before I came of getting some of the stuff out and getting ready to gut it out, you know like cut out where the water — well the water was probably to my waist, about three and a half to four feet. And when I go back next week that’s a project that I’m going to deal with. To try to deal with that. And after the hurricane season is over then I’ll see about what am I going to do whether I’m going to repair it or sell it or move out. And like my wife wants to go back to New Orleans but I can live anywhere. I could live up here if it wasn’t the cold weather. ‘Cause somebody, they offered me a gig around Boston but I wouldn’t even tell her that because that cold weather, I wouldn’t even mention that to her.
